budget_items.what_was_said: Members proposed discussing the parameters of the prudent investor rule, adopted by Lunenburg at a 2024 special town meeting, as it applies to trust fund management.
Members proposed reviewing whether the treasurer and finance director use mark-to-market accounting referencing yield and daily rates rather than only quarterly and annual figures.
Members discussed showing the public a clip of the investment firm's prior presentation to the budget task force rather than having the firm appear again.
Members proposed reviewing how requests to use expendable trust funds are handled, including penalties for early withdrawal and the impact of large withdrawals on the rate of return.

minutes.headline: Two elected members organized as chair and vice chair despite a dispute over how the meeting was convened
minutes.summary: A newly elected member of the Trust Fund Commission opened and closed the meeting with a lengthy objection that the assistant town clerk's convening of the meeting, on an agenda substituted by the town manager, violated separation-of-powers principles under Massachusetts law. Despite the objection, the two elected members elected John Bowen as chairman and Richard Howard as vice chairman, set a regular meeting schedule (second and fourth Thursdays, 5:00-6:30 PM) with the next meeting for July 10, 2025, and outlined a list of trust-fund investment and policy topics to take up then. No members of the public offered comment, and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The two elected members elected a chairman and vice chairman despite one member's objection that the meeting's convening violated separation-of-powers law.
The objecting member argued at length that the assistant town clerk convening the meeting, on an agenda substituted by the town manager, improperly asserted executive authority over the board.
Members agreed in advance by email on a six-item list of trust-fund topics -- including the prudent investor rule and a withdrawal policy -- for the next meeting's agenda.
The commission set a regular meeting schedule of the second and fourth Thursdays and scheduled its next meeting for July 10, 2025.
No members of the public offered comment before adjournment.

why_it_matters: The Trust Fund Commission oversees how the town's trust funds are invested and drawn down, so the policy items it plans to take up -- withdrawal rules, accounting methods, portfolio allocation -- can affect how much of those funds is available and when.
The objection raised at the meeting concerns which town official has authority to convene and set the agenda for an elected board, a governance question separate from any single vote taken.
